# Cryptic Teacher

**[cryptic.paultarjan.com](https://cryptic.paultarjan.com)**

A static web app, with no framework and no backend, that teaches you to solve
cryptic crosswords. It uses real published puzzles and gives each clue an
escalating **hint ladder** instead of a bare answer key. The rungs, in ladder
order:

<!-- LADDER-START generated by tools/build_readme.py — do not edit -->
1. **Spot the indicator words** — the anagram, container, reversal and homophone signal words are highlighted.
2. **Where is the definition?** — the definition part of the clue is highlighted.
3. **What kind of clue is this?** — anagram? charade? container? hidden word? …
4. **The building blocks** — the fodder and the synonym breakdown, a piece at a time (“host = ARMY; part of TV duo = ANT”). A double definition has none: its halves are the definition rung's.
5. **Full walkthrough** — the whole assembly, step by step.

**Fill in answer** writes the solution into the grid. It is the way out of a clue rather than a step in it, so it is offered alongside the rungs once the building blocks are up, and it is not counted as one.
<!-- LADDER-END -->

Each rung asks before it tells: tap the words you think are the definition or
the indicator, and you get the rung free if you are right. The rest of the
site has letter reveals, grid checks, a glossary of abbreviations, a list of
indicators, a short tutorial at /learn/, and progress saved in your browser.
[docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md) has the details.

<!-- CORPUS-START generated by tools/build_readme.py — do not edit -->
**Corpus** — about 51,000 puzzles across 25 series (Times cryptic 11,000, Guardian cryptic 8,800, Financial Times cryptic 5,600, Telegraph cryptic 5,500, Independent daily 4,000, Telegraph Toughie 3,600, Times Quick Cryptic 3,100, Guardian Quiptic 1,400, Observer Everyman 1,200, scanned book reprints 1,100, Sunday Telegraph cryptic 910, Independent Sunday 730, Observer Azed 690, Sunday Times cryptic 600, Private Eye Cyclops 530, Times Jumbo 530, Canberra Times cryptic 460, Times Mephisto 440, Sunday Telegraph Toughie 240, The Nation cryptic 220, Times Club Monthly Special 130, Guardian Genius 130, Metro cryptic 80, TLS crossword 50, Listener crossword 20). About 17,000 of them are annotated clue-for-clue, all six rungs, machine-validated: about 35% of 1,500,000 clues. The rest are backlog the daily job is still draining. About 21,000 of those carry hints marked up from a solving blog's write-up (definitions, clue types, pieces) and are badged <em>hints via</em> that blog; the other 14,000 show an <em>answers only</em> badge and degrade gracefully (checking and letter reveals still work; the teaching ladder appears once a puzzle is annotated).
<!-- CORPUS-END -->

## Run it locally

The puzzle list and the script form of each puzzle are generated from the
committed puzzle files. After a fresh clone, build them once (about ten
seconds):

```
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py --reindex
```

Then open `index.html` in a browser (it works from `file://`), or run
`python3 -m http.server 8017` in the repo root and visit
<http://localhost:8017/>. Re-run the reindex after you fetch or annotate
anything.

## Contributing

Bad hints are the most useful thing to report: every clue on the site has a
**Report a bad hint** button. To add a puzzle, fetch it, annotate it by hand
or with Claude Code using `tools/annotate_prompt.md`, then validate it:

```
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py 30123
python3 tools/validate_annotations.py 30123
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py --reindex
```

[docs/ADDING_PUZZLES.md](docs/ADDING_PUZZLES.md) covers the other papers and
the full set of checks.

## Credits

Puzzle grids and clues remain the copyright of their publishers. The
publishers are listed per series in `tools/series.py`. Puzzles are fetched from
the publishers' own sites, archives and books. Each clue is reproduced
alongside original commentary that explains how it works: hints, a
walkthrough of its wordplay and tutorials. That is use for criticism,
review, teaching and research, which we believe is fair use under US law
and fair dealing under Canadian and UK law. All annotations, hints and
tutorial content are original to this project. A rights holder who would
rather their puzzles were not included can open an issue on this
repository, and they will be taken down. This
project is not affiliated with any publisher.
